nodes.name: Ni₀.₉Co₀.₁(OH)₂ ECI deposition
nodes.procedure: Nickel foam substrates (Ni-4753; RECEMAT; 3 mm thickness; 400-μm pores; 95.2% porosity; 5,400 m² m⁻³ specific surface) were cut into 1 cm × 2 cm pieces. The substrates were dipped in acetone and ethanol, cleaned ultrasonically in isopropanol for 15 min, and then washed with deionized water. Before deposition, the substrates were vacuum immersed in the deposition solution for 30 min by placing the substrates in a vacuum chamber (Struers Epovac) and flooding them with the deposition solution. The deposition solution was composed of nickel nitrate, sodium nitrite and cobalt nitrate in an aqueous mixture of ethanol in water, titrated to an initial pH of 4 with nitric acid. A portion of 1 cm × 1 cm of each nickel foam substrate was dipped in the deposition solution, and the remaining portion was used as the electrical contact. Each substrate was connected as the cathode to a potentiostat and placed between two nickel foam pieces acting as anodes. Deposition was carried out at a constant temperature of 80 °C, by applying a cathodic current of 60 mA. After deposition, each electrode was washed thoroughly with deionized water.

nodes.name: NiFe LDH electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The same nickel foam substrate described... was used for the fabrication of the NiFe LDH anode. The deposition solution comprised 0.095 M Ni(NO₃)₂ and 0.05 M FeCl₂ in deionized water. Before deposition, the solution was purged with N₂ gas for 20 min. The same cell configuration described... was also employed for NiFe LDH anode fabrication. Deposition was carried out by applying a pulsed cathodic current of 10 mA for 20 cycles of 2 s on/off pulses, following the methods described elsewhere⁴⁹. Following deposition, the anode was washed in deionized water.
